newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES FIRM, DEMAND SLACKENS.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES FIRM, DEMAND SLACKENS.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates firmed on Tuesday, although fresh kuna demand slackened after the panic over pension payments, money market dealers said.
New borrowings fell to 22.5 million kuna ($3.4 million) by 0900 GMT from Monday's 35 million, leaving a comfortable 30-million surplus.
"Supply has fallen slightly (compared to last week), but the situation is still not drastic," said a dealer.
Interbank call money funds were granted at a flat 7.0 percent and one-month at 12 percent, up one percentage point.
Savings banks also paid a higher 14 percent for one-month and 18-percent for two-month kuna.
As their balances rose again to 644 million kuna at the end of Monday, some banks repaid 34 million in call money loans, raised last week ahead of the July pension payment.
They were still said to be complaining about strained liquidity and were eager to sell the hard currency bought from foreign tourists to the central bank.
But the central bank said it would not intervene this week because of ample kuna funds on the market. None of the banks took out any Lombard loans, an official told Reuters.

Only one bank borrowed money in overnight trade on Monday to cover a tiny shortfall and another bought 50 million kuna for mandatory reserve. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.575 Croatian Kuna)
